source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων τοῖς δώδεκα μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, μετέβη ἐκεῖθεν τοῦ διδάσκειν καὶ κηρύσσειν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus commanding the twelve disciples of him, he moved on from there to teach and to preach in the cities of them.

en.L: And it happened, when Jesus had finished instructing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on from there to teach and to preach in their towns.
en.B: When Jesus had finished giving these instructions to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved on from there to teach and to proclaim the message in their towns.
en.R: Jesus finished telling {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers what to do. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place and went to teach and preach in the towns of that area.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Jesús terminó de dar instrucciones a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos, se fue de allí para enseñar y predicar en las ciudades de ellos.
es.B: Cuando Jesús terminó de dar estas instrucciones a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos, se fue de allí a enseñar y a anunciar el mensaje en las ciudades de ellos.
es.R: Jesús terminó de decirles a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce seguidores lo que tenían que hacer. Después se fue de allí a enseñar y a predicar en los pueblos de aquella región.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Jésus eut achevé de donner des instructions à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partit de là pour enseigner et prêcher dans leurs villes.
fr.B: Lorsque Jésus eut fini de donner ces instructions à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partit de là pour enseigner et annoncer le message dans leurs villes.
fr.R: Jésus a fini de dire à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples ce qu’ils devaient faire. Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est parti de là, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé enseigner et prêcher dans les villes de la région.

sw.L: Na ikatokea kwamba, Yesu alipomaliza kuwapa maagizo wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili, akapita kutoka pale ili kufundisha na kuhubiri katika miji yao.
sw.B: Yesu alipomaliza kuwapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili maagizo hayo, aliondoka mahali hapo, akaenda kufundisha na kutangaza ujumbe katika miji yao.
sw.R: Yesu alimaliza kuwaeleza wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili mambo ya kufanya. Kisha akaondoka pale, akaenda kufundisha na kuhubiri katika miji ya eneo lile.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là, khi Đức Giê-xu đã dặn bảo mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi đó để dạy dỗ và rao giảng trong các thành của họ.
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu đã dặn bảo mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời nơi ấy để đi dạy dỗ và rao giảng sứ điệp trong các thành của họ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu dặn bảo mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời nơi đó, đi dạy dỗ và rao giảng trong các thành của vùng ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 자기의 열두 제자에게 지시하기를 마치셨을 때에 [이런 일이 있었다]. 그분이 그들의 도시들에서 가르치시고 선포하시려고 거기에서 떠나가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 열두 제자에게 이렇게 지시하기를 마치시고, 그곳을 떠나 여러 고을에서 가르치시며 말씀을 선포하셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 열두 제자에게 해야 할 일을 다 일러 주셨다. 그리고 그곳을 떠나 그 지역의 여러 마을로 가셔서 사람들을 가르치시고 하나님의 말씀을 전하셨다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando Jesus terminou de dar instruções aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze discípulos, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} partiu dali para ensinar e pregar nas cidades deles.
pt.B: Quando Jesus terminou de dar essas instruções aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze discípulos, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} partiu dali para ensinar e anunciar a mensagem nas cidades deles.
pt.R: Jesus terminou de explicar aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze seguidores o que eles deviam fazer. Depois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} saiu daquele lugar e foi ensinar e pregar nas cidades daquela região.

am.L: እንዲህም ሆነ፤ ኢየሱስ አሥራ ሁለቱን ደቀ መዛሙርቱን ማዘዝ በፈጸመ ጊዜ፣ በከተሞቻቸው ለማስተማርና ለመስበክ ከዚያ ተነሥቶ ሄደ።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ለአሥራ ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ይህን መመሪያ ሰጥቶ ከጨረሰ በኋላ፣ በከተሞቻቸው ለማስተማርና መልእክቱን ለማወጅ ከዚያ ተነሥቶ ሄደ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ለአሥራ ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ምን ማድረግ እንዳለባቸው ነግሮ ጨረሰ። ከዚያም ያን ቦታ ትቶ በአካባቢው ባሉ ከተሞች ለማስተማርና ለመስበክ ሄደ።

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished: the formula that closes the second long speech
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (7:28; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1). This one closes the instructions of chapter 10.

decisions.choice: their towns: the towns of the Jewish people of the region
decisions.reason: "Their" has no clear antecedent; it most likely means the people of Galilee, as in 4:23 and 9:35 ("their synagogues"). Matthew does not say here that the twelve set out.

decisions.choice: proclaim the message (B); the towns of that area (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what was proclaimed; Readable says which towns are meant.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}}
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("se fue"), where there is nothing to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: en las ciudades de ellos
decisions.reason: "Their towns" are the towns of the people of the region (meaning decision m2). "Sus ciudades" could be read as Jesus's own.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Gospels: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and taught. Jesus's words about John (11:7-19) keep the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}; no span on the verbs
decisions.reason: The English "he" and "his" take the setting. Swahili carries the subject in the verb prefix (akaenda), which cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives take the span, as in John. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "Và xảy ra là" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the formula that closes Jesus's second long speech (meaning decision), as in 9:10.

decisions.choice: "마치셨을 때에" kept as the closing formula of the speech; no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 11
alternatives: merging the formula into the next clause at Literal
decisions.reason: "When Jesus had finished" is Matthew's formula that closes each long speech (meaning decision); Literal keeps "and it happened" with a bracketed clause, so the formula stands as its own unit. Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시-, 께서 and 그분 (docs/korean-style.md section 7).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns (እርሱ, እሱ, አንተ, the verb endings) are written once, with no span.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης ἀκούσας ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ χριστοῦ πέμψας διὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν;

records.literal_gloss: And John having heard in the prison the works of the Christ, having sent through the disciples of him, \v 3 said to him, You are the coming [one] or another are we to expect?

en.L: Now John, having heard in prison about the works of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, sent [word] through his disciples \v 3 [and] said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or are we to look for another?"
en.B: Meanwhile John, now in prison, heard about the works of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. He sent word by his disciples \v 3 and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or should we wait for someone else?"
en.R: John the Baptist was in prison. He heard about the things the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was doing. So he sent some of his followers to Jesus. \v 3 They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one God promised to send? Or should we wait for someone else?"

es.L: Y Juan, habiendo oído en la cárcel las obras del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, envió [aviso] por medio de sus discípulos \v 3 [y] {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el que viene, o debemos esperar a otro?».
es.B: Entretanto Juan, que estaba en la cárcel, oyó hablar de las obras del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}. Envió un mensaje por medio de sus discípulos \v 3 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el que iba a venir, o debemos esperar a otro?».
es.R: Juan el Bautista estaba en la cárcel. Allí oyó lo que estaba haciendo el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}. Entonces envió a algunos de sus seguidores a Jesús. \v 3 Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el que Dios prometió enviar? ¿O debemos esperar a otro?».

fr.L: Or Jean, ayant entendu parler, dans la prison, des œuvres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, envoya [un message] par ses disciples \v 3 et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui qui vient, ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ? »
fr.B: Jean, qui était alors en prison, entendit parler des œuvres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Il envoya ses disciples \v 3 {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui qui doit venir, ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ? »
fr.R: Jean le Baptiste était en prison. Il a entendu parler de ce que faisait le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Alors il a envoyé quelques-uns de ses disciples auprès de Jésus. \v 3 Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui que Dieu a promis d’envoyer ? Ou devons-nous attendre quelqu’un d’autre ? »

sw.L: Basi Yohana, aliposikia gerezani kazi za {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, akatuma [ujumbe] kupitia wanafunzi wake, \v 3 akamwambia, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiye yule anayekuja, au tumtarajie mwingine?"
sw.B: Wakati huo Yohana alikuwa gerezani, akasikia habari za kazi za {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Akatuma ujumbe kupitia wanafunzi wake, \v 3 akamwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiye yule anayekuja, au tumsubiri mtu mwingine?"
sw.R: Yohana Mbatizaji alikuwa gerezani. Alisikia habari za mambo ambayo {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikuwa akifanya. Kwa hiyo aliwatuma baadhi ya wafuasi wake kwa Yesu. \v 3 Walimwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiye yule ambaye Mungu aliahidi kumtuma? Au tumsubiri mtu mwingine?"

vi.L: Còn Giăng, ở trong ngục nghe về các việc của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, thì sai các môn đồ mình \v 3 đến nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thầy có phải là Đấng phải đến, hay chúng tôi phải chờ đợi một đấng khác?"
vi.B: Lúc ấy Giăng đang ở trong ngục. Nghe nói về các việc {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} làm, ông sai các môn đồ mình đến \v 3 hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thầy có phải là Đấng phải đến không, hay chúng tôi phải đợi một đấng khác?"
vi.R: Giăng Báp-tít đang ở trong tù. Ông nghe nói về những việc {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đang làm. Vì vậy, ông sai mấy môn đồ của mình đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. \v 3 Họ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thầy có phải là Đấng mà Đức Chúa Trời đã hứa sai đến không? Hay chúng tôi phải đợi một người khác?"

ko.L: 그런데 요한이 감옥에서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 일들에 대해 듣고, 자기 제자들을 통해 [사람을] 보내어 \v 3 그분께 말했다. "선생님께서 오실 그분이십니까, 아니면 저희가 다른 분을 기다려야 합니까?"
ko.B: 그때 요한은 감옥에 있었는데, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 하신 일들에 대한 소식을 들었다. 그래서 자기 제자들을 보내어 \v 3 예수께 여쭈었다. "선생님께서 오시기로 되어 있는 그분이십니까, 아니면 저희가 다른 분을 기다려야 합니까?"
ko.R: 그때 세례자 요한은 감옥에 갇혀 있었다. 요한은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 하시는 일들에 대해 들었다. 그래서 자기 제자들 몇 사람을 예수께 보냈다. \v 3 그들이 예수께 여쭈었다. "선생님께서 하나님이 보내 주시겠다고 약속하신 바로 그분이십니까? 아니면 저희가 다른 분을 기다려야 합니까?"

pt.L: Ora, João, tendo ouvido na prisão sobre as obras do {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, mandou [recado] por meio dos próprios discípulos \v 3 [e] {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "És {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} o que vem, ou devemos aguardar outro?"
pt.B: Enquanto isso, João, que estava na prisão, ouviu falar das obras do {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}. Ele mandou recado por meio dos seus discípulos \v 3 e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntou: "És {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} aquele que há de vir, ou devemos esperar por outra pessoa?"
pt.R: João Batista estava na prisão. Ele ouviu falar das coisas que o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} estava fazendo. Então mandou alguns dos seus seguidores até Jesus. \v 3 Eles perguntaram a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "És {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} aquele que Deus prometeu enviar? Ou devemos esperar outra pessoa?"

am.L: ዮሐንስም በእስር ቤት ሆኖ {{christos:የክርስቶስ|የመሲሑ}} ሥራዎችን ሰምቶ፣ በደቀ መዛሙርቱ በኩል [መልእክት] ልኮ \v 3 እንዲህ አለው፦ «የሚመጣው አንተ ነህ ወይስ ሌላውን እንጠባበቅ?»
am.B: በዚህ መካከል በእስር ቤት የነበረው ዮሐንስ {{christos:የክርስቶስ|የመሲሑ}} ሥራዎችን ሰማ። በደቀ መዛሙርቱም በኩል መልእክት ልኮ \v 3 እንዲህ ሲል ጠየቀው፦ «የሚመጣው አንተ ነህ ወይስ ሌላ ሰው እንጠብቅ?»
am.R: መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ በእስር ቤት ነበር። {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሑ}} የሚያደርገውን ነገር ሰማ። ስለዚህ አንዳንድ ደቀ መዛሙርቱን ወደ ኢየሱስ ላከ። \v 3 እነርሱም እንዲህ ብለው ጠየቁት፦ «እግዚአብሔር እልካለሁ ብሎ ተስፋ የሰጠው አንተ ነህ? ወይስ ሌላ ሰው እንጠብቅ?»

decisions.choice: in prison: John had been arrested by Herod Antipas
decisions.reason: Matthew mentions John's arrest in 4:12 and tells its cause in 14:3-5. The Jewish historian Josephus places the prison at the fortress of Machaerus, east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the works of the Christ: what Jesus had been doing, told in chapters 8-9
alternatives: works John had heard of only by rumor
decisions.reason: Matthew, the narrator, calls them the Messiah's works. John asks whether they mean what he hopes. The same word returns in 11:19 ("her deeds").

decisions.choice: the one who is coming: the one John had announced
decisions.reason: John had said "the one who comes after me" (3:11). The phrase echoes Psalm 118:26 and Malachi 3:1, where the coming one brings God's judgment and salvation.

decisions.choice: through his disciples, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: two of his disciples, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The two Greek words differ by a letter or two; many later manuscripts read "two", perhaps under the influence of Luke 7:18-19. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the one who is coming" meant to John and his hearers.

decisions.choice: ses disciples (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; French keeps "disciples" for John's disciples too, as in Luke 7:18.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" for "the Christ"
decisions.reason: The christos setting as the style guide gives it; Matthew uses the title with the article here, so it stands alone, without the name.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" and "chúng tôi" in the question of John's disciples
decisions.reason: As in 9:14: John's disciples ask Jesus as a teacher and are not his own disciples, so they use the respectful noun of address and "chúng tôi". "Đấng phải đến" is capitalised because it names the one John had announced (meaning decision); "một đấng khác" is not.

decisions.choice: John's question in 합쇼체 with "선생님" for "you" and "저희" for "we"
decisions.reason: People speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 (docs/korean-style.md section 4); Korean does not address a respected teacher as "당신", so "선생님" stands for the pronoun, as in the Korean Mark 5:31, and Literal does not bracket it.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} with "의" (L) or "께서" (B, R) after the span
decisions.reason: The style guide's span for Christos; the particles after it fit both forms.

decisions.choice: És tu (tu)
decisions.reason: John's question is addressed to Jesus, so it uses "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the inverted "És tu ...?" is the ordinary written form of the question.

records.literal_gloss: Blind receive sight and lame walk, lepers are cleansed and deaf hear, and dead are raised and poor are told good news;

en.L: [the] blind receive sight and [the] lame walk, lepers are cleansed and [the] deaf hear, and [the] dead are raised and [the] poor have good news proclaimed [to them].
en.B: the blind can see and the lame are walking, people with leprosy are made clean and the deaf can hear, the dead are raised to life, and the poor are hearing the good news.
en.R: Blind people can see again. People who could not walk are walking. People with bad skin diseases are healed. Deaf people can hear. Dead people are brought back to life. And poor people are hearing the good news.

es.L: [los] ciegos recobran la vista y [los] cojos caminan, [los] leprosos quedan limpios y [los] sordos oyen, y [los] muertos son levantados y a [los] pobres se les anuncia la buena noticia;
es.B: los ciegos ven, los cojos caminan, los que tienen lepra quedan limpios, los sordos oyen, los muertos resucitan y los pobres escuchan la buena noticia.
es.R: Los ciegos pueden ver otra vez. Los que no podían caminar están caminando. Los que tenían enfermedades graves de la piel son sanados. Los sordos pueden oír. Los muertos vuelven a la vida. Y los pobres escuchan la buena noticia.

fr.L: des aveugles recouvrent la vue et des boiteux marchent, des lépreux sont purifiés et des sourds entendent, et des morts sont ressuscités et à des pauvres la bonne nouvelle est annoncée.
fr.B: les aveugles voient, les boiteux marchent, les lépreux sont rendus purs, les sourds entendent, les morts reviennent à la vie, et les pauvres entendent la bonne nouvelle.
fr.R: Les aveugles voient de nouveau. Ceux qui ne pouvaient pas marcher marchent. Les gens qui avaient de graves maladies de peau sont guéris. Les sourds entendent. Les morts reviennent à la vie. Et les pauvres entendent la bonne nouvelle.

decisions.choice: the signs Isaiah promised for the time when God comes to save
alternatives: a simple report with no background
decisions.reason: Isaiah 35:5-6 promises that the blind will see, the deaf hear and the lame leap; 26:19 that the dead will live; and 61:1 that good news will be brought to the poor. Jesus answers John with Scripture.

decisions.choice: each of these has happened in chapters 8-9
alternatives: only a promise for the future
decisions.reason: Lepers (8:2-3), the lame (9:2-7), the dead (9:18-25), the blind (9:27-30) and one who could not speak (9:32-33).

decisions.choice: deaf: those who cannot hear
decisions.reason: The word can mean either (in 9:32 it means unable to speak). Here it is paired with "hear", as in Isaiah 35:5.

decisions.choice: have good news proclaimed (L); are hearing the good news (B, R)
alternatives: have the gospel preached to them
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Isaiah 61:1 uses in the Greek version. "Good news" keeps that echo and suits every level.

decisions.choice: se les anuncia la buena noticia (L); escuchan la buena noticia (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the telling of good news, not the name of the message, so every level says "la buena noticia", as the English says "good news".

decisions.choice: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: The English says "good news" at every level to keep the echo of Isaiah 61:1, so French does too, as in Luke 7:22.

decisions.choice: habari njema, at every level
decisions.reason: The verb is the telling of good news, not the name of the message, so every level says "habari njema", as the English says "good news".

decisions.choice: "được nghe rao giảng Tin Lành" (L); "được nghe Tin Lành" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "to be told good news"; "Tin Lành" is the settled word at every level, Readable included, as in Mark 13:10.

decisions.choice: "듣지 못하는 사람" for the deaf; leprosy as in 10:8; "복음" (L, B), "기쁜 소식" (R)
decisions.reason: Older Korean names for the deaf and the lame are now felt to be demeaning, so the people are described by what they could not do. Gospel is a key term, "복음" at Literal and Balanced and "기쁜 소식" at Readable, through Matthew.

decisions.choice: boas-novas, at every level
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "good news" here to echo Isaiah 61:1, Portuguese says "boas-novas" at every level (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6). "São evangelizados" sounds like church jargon.

decisions.choice: ዓይነ ስውሮች (the blind); መስማት የተሳናቸው (the deaf)
decisions.reason: ዕውር and ደንቆሮ are the old words, but today they are heard as insults; ዓይነ ስውር and መስማት የተሳነው are the ordinary respectful words and say exactly the same.

decisions.choice: stumble over me: be offended by Jesus and so fall away
alternatives: be led into sin by me
decisions.reason: The verb pictures tripping over an obstacle. Jesus was not the kind of Messiah many expected; John himself had spoken of fire and judgment (3:10-12).

decisions.choice: blessed: favored by God, as in 5:3-11
decisions.reason: The same word begins each saying in 5:3-11.

decisions.choice: is not upset by what I do and does not turn away from me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of stumbling.

decisions.choice: dichoso
decisions.reason: Favored by God (meaning decision m2). "Bienaventurado" is the traditional church word but sounds old to many readers; "feliz" can sound like a mood. "Dichoso" is current and keeps the sense of good fortune given.

decisions.choice: heureux at every level
decisions.reason: As in the Beatitudes (5:3-11) and Luke 7:23: "heureux" is the settled French word for this blessing.

decisions.choice: "Phước [cho]" (L), "Phước cho" (B), "Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho" (R); "vấp ngã vì Ta" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Blessed means favored by God (meaning decision), worded as John 20:29. To stumble over Jesus is to be offended by him and so fall away (meaning decision); "vấp ngã" keeps the picture and the falling away.

decisions.choice: "복이 있다"; "걸려 넘어지다" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Blessed is favored by God (meaning decision), which "복이 있다" says; "행복하다" is a feeling. "걸려 넘어지다" is the Korean John's and Mark's picture for being offended and falling away (John 16:1; Mark 14:27); Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: የተባረከ (blessed)
decisions.reason: As in the Beatitudes, የተባረከ says that God favours the person, in a word every reader knows; ብፁዕ is the church's Ge'ez word, and ደስተኛ describes a feeling.

es.B: Sí, por cierto, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo, y es todavía más que un profeta.
es.R: Sí, Juan es un profeta. Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que es todavía más que un profeta.

fr.L: Oui, je vous le dis, et plus qu’un prophète.
fr.B: Oui, je vous le dis, il est même bien plus qu’un prophète.
fr.R: Oui, c’est un prophète. Mais je vous le dis, il est encore plus qu’un prophète.

sw.L: Ndiyo, nawaambia, na [mtu] zaidi ya nabii.
sw.B: Ndiyo kweli, nawaambia, na yeye ni zaidi hata ya nabii.
sw.R: Ndiyo, yeye ni nabii. Lakini nawaambia, yeye ni zaidi hata ya nabii.

vi.L: Phải, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, và [người ấy] còn hơn một nhà tiên tri.
vi.B: Đúng vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, ông ấy còn hơn cả một nhà tiên tri nữa.
vi.R: Đúng, ông ấy là một nhà tiên tri. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, ông ấy còn lớn hơn một nhà tiên tri nữa.

ko.L: 그렇다. 내가 너희에게 말한다. 예언자보다 더 나은 사람이다.
ko.B: 그렇다. 내가 너희에게 말한다. 그는 예언자보다 더 큰 사람이다.
ko.R: 그렇다. 요한은 예언자다. 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 요한은 예언자보다 더 큰 사람이다.

pt.L: Sim, eu lhes digo, e mais do que profeta.
pt.B: Sim, de fato, eu lhes digo: ele é até mais do que um profeta.
pt.R: Sim, ele é um profeta. Mas eu digo a vocês: ele é ainda mais do que um profeta.

am.L: አዎን፣ እላችኋለሁ፤ ከነቢይም የሚበልጥ [ነው]።
am.B: አዎን፣ እላችኋለሁ፤ እርሱ ከነቢይ እንኳ ይበልጣል።
am.R: አዎ፣ እርሱ ነቢይ ነው። ነገር ግን እላችኋለሁ፤ ከነቢይ እንኳ ይበልጣል።

decisions.choice: more than a prophet: John is the messenger the prophets foretold
alternatives: a greater speaker than the prophets
decisions.reason: Other prophets spoke of the coming day; John was himself spoken of, as 11:10 shows.

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.

records.literal_gloss: This is about whom it has been written: Behold, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you before you.

en.L: This is [the one] about whom it is written: 'Look, I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'
en.B: This is the man of whom Scripture says, 'I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make ready {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'
en.R: John is the one the Scriptures were talking about when God said, 'I will send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will prepare the way for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

es.L: Este es [aquel] de quien está escrito: “Mira, envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} rostro; él preparará {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} camino delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}”.
es.B: Este es el hombre de quien dice la Escritura: “Envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; él dejará listo {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} camino por delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}”.
es.R: Juan es aquel de quien hablaban las Escrituras cuando Dios dijo: “Enviaré a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Él preparará el camino para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}”.

fr.L: Celui-ci est [celui] dont il est écrit : “Voici, j’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face, qui préparera {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.”
fr.B: C’est de lui que l’Écriture dit : “J’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; il préparera {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.”
fr.R: Jean est celui dont parlent les Écritures, quand Dieu dit : “J’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Il préparera la route pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.”

sw.L: Huyu ndiye ambaye kumeandikwa juu yake, 'Angalia, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninampeleka mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mbele ya uso {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, naye ataiandaa njia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.'
sw.B: Huyu ndiye mtu ambaye Maandiko yanasema habari zake, 'Ninamtuma mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} akutangulie; yeye ataiandaa njia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.'
sw.R: Yohana ndiye yule ambaye Maandiko yalisema habari zake, Mungu aliposema, 'Nitamtuma mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} akutangulie. Yeye atakuandalia njia.'

vi.L: Đây là [người] mà về người ấy đã có chép: 'Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai sứ giả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi trước mặt Con, là người sẽ dọn đường của Con trước Con.'
vi.B: Kinh Thánh đã chép về ông ấy: 'Ta sai sứ giả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi trước Con; người ấy sẽ dọn đường cho Con đi.'
vi.R: Giăng chính là người mà Kinh Thánh đã nói đến, khi Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Ta sẽ sai sứ giả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi trước Con. Người ấy sẽ dọn đường sẵn cho Con.'

ko.L: 이 사람은 그에 대해 기록된 그 사람이다. '보라, 내가 내 사자를 네 얼굴 앞에 보낸다. 그가 네 앞에서 네 길을 마련할 것이다.'
ko.B: 성경에 이렇게 기록된 사람이 바로 요한이다. '보라, 내가 내 사자를 너보다 앞서 보낸다. 그가 네 앞에서 네 길을 닦아 놓을 것이다.'
ko.R: 성경이 말하는 사람이 바로 요한이다. 하나님께서 이렇게 말씀하셨다. '보라! 내가 내 심부름꾼을 너보다 먼저 보낸다. 그가 너를 위해 길을 준비할 것이다.'

pt.L: Este é [aquele] de quem está escrito: 'Eis que eu envio o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} mensageiro diante da {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} face, e ele preparará o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} caminho à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} frente.'
pt.B: Este é o homem de quem a Escritura diz: 'Estou enviando o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} mensageiro à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} frente; ele vai aprontar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} caminho adiante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.'
pt.R: João é aquele de quem as Escrituras falavam quando Deus disse: 'Vou enviar o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} mensageiro à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} frente. Ele vai preparar o caminho para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.'

am.L: ይህ ስለ እርሱ እንዲህ ተብሎ የተጻፈለት ነው፦ “እነሆ፣ እኔ በፊትህ መንገድህን የሚያዘጋጀውን መልእክተኛዬን ከፊትህ እልካለሁ።”
am.B: መጽሐፍ እንዲህ የሚለው ስለዚህ ሰው ነው፦ “መልእክተኛዬን ከአንተ አስቀድሜ እልካለሁ፤ እርሱም በፊትህ መንገድህን ያዘጋጃል።”
am.R: ቅዱሳት መጻሕፍት ስለ ዮሐንስ ሲናገሩ እግዚአብሔር እንዲህ ብሏል፦ “መልእክተኛዬን ከአንተ በፊት እልካለሁ። እሱም መንገድህን ያዘጋጅልሃል።”

decisions.choice: Malachi 3:1, joined with Exodus 23:20
decisions.reason: "I am sending my messenger before your face" matches the Greek of Exodus 23:20, where God sends his angel ahead of Israel. "He will prepare the way" is from Malachi 3:1, where the messenger goes before God himself.

decisions.choice: your: the one for whom the way is prepared is Jesus
decisions.reason: In Malachi the messenger prepares the way "before me", that is, before God. Here God speaks to another, the one who comes, and the coming of God is the coming of Jesus.

decisions.choice: messenger: one sent with a message
decisions.reason: The word can mean either. Here it is John, a human messenger.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: when God said
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, since "my" and "I" in the quotation are God.

decisions.choice: "j’envoie" without a span; "mon" (God), "ta", "ton", "toi" (Jesus) with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in Luke 7:27: God speaks and the way is prepared for Jesus (m2), so every pronoun for either takes the setting; the first-person subject "je" never does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} for God; {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} for the one addressed
decisions.reason: God speaks, and the one he speaks to is Jesus (meaning decision m2), so the free pronouns and possessives for both take the setting. The English leaves "I" plain; Swahili "mimi" is a free pronoun and takes it, as in John.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and speaks to the one who comes as "Con", capitalised, with no setting span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:2, where the same words of Malachi 3:1 stand. The one for whom the way is prepared is Jesus (meaning decision); God speaks to him as Son, so "Con" is a noun of address and takes no span, while God's own "Ta" mid-sentence carries the setting.

decisions.choice: the quotation worded as in the Korean Mark 1:2, with "네 앞에서" added for Matthew's "before you"; "사자" (L, B), "심부름꾼" (R); "너" in the quotation
decisions.reason: Mark quotes the same words of Malachi 3:1 (meaning decision), so the Korean keeps the Korean Mark's wording, except that "behold" is "보라", as through the Korean Matthew. God speaks in the plain style to the one whose way is prepared, as in the Korean Mark; that one is Jesus (meaning decision), but the quotation keeps the prophet's "너".

decisions.choice: tua, teu, ti
decisions.reason: In the quotation God speaks to the one who is coming, whom the meaning note (m2) identifies as Jesus, so Portuguese uses "tu", as for God's speech throughout (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); each pronoun carries the deity_pronoun setting, as in the English.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ ἐγήγερται ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν μείζων Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, not has arisen among born of women greater than John the Baptist; the but lesser in the kingdom of the heavens greater than him is.

en.L: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has not arisen [anyone] greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of the heavens is greater than he.
en.B: Truly I tell you, of all who have ever been born of women, no one has appeared who is greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the smallest in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is.
en.R: I tell you the truth, no one who has ever lived is greater than John the Baptist. But even the least important person in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John.

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: entre los nacidos de mujeres no ha surgido [nadie] más grande que Juan el Bautista; pero el menor en el reino de los cielos es más grande que él.
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que, de todos los que han nacido de mujer, no ha aparecido nadie más grande que Juan el Bautista. Sin embargo, aun el más pequeño en el reino de los cielos es más grande que él.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: nadie que haya vivido jamás es más grande que Juan el Bautista. Pero hasta la persona menos importante en el reino de los cielos es más grande que Juan.

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis, parmi ceux qui sont nés de femmes, il ne s’est levé [personne] de plus grand que Jean le Baptiste ; mais le plus petit dans le royaume des cieux est plus grand que lui.
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis, de tous les êtres nés d’une femme, aucun n’a paru qui soit plus grand que Jean le Baptiste. Pourtant, le plus petit dans le royaume des cieux est plus grand que lui.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : aucun être humain n’a jamais été plus grand que Jean le Baptiste. Mais même celui qui est le moins important dans le royaume des cieux est plus grand que Jean.

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia, miongoni mwa waliozaliwa na wanawake hajainuka [mtu] mkuu kuliko Yohana Mbatizaji; lakini aliye mdogo zaidi katika ufalme wa mbinguni ni mkuu kumzidi yeye.
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, kati ya wote waliozaliwa na wanawake hajatokea mtu aliye mkuu kuliko Yohana Mbatizaji. Hata hivyo, hata yule aliye mdogo kabisa katika ufalme wa mbinguni ni mkuu kuliko yeye.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli, hakuna mtu aliyewahi kuishi aliye mkuu kuliko Yohana Mbatizaji. Lakini hata mtu asiye muhimu kabisa katika ufalme wa mbinguni ni mkuu kuliko Yohana.

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, trong những người do phụ nữ sinh ra, chưa từng có ai lớn hơn Giăng Báp-tít; nhưng người nhỏ nhất trong vương quốc thiên đàng còn lớn hơn ông.
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, trong tất cả những người do phụ nữ sinh ra, chưa từng có ai lớn hơn Giăng Báp-tít. Thế nhưng người nhỏ nhất trong vương quốc thiên đàng còn lớn hơn ông.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các người, trong mọi người đã từng sống trên đời, chưa có ai lớn hơn Giăng Báp-tít. Nhưng người kém quan trọng nhất trong vương quốc thiên đàng lại lớn hơn Giăng.

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 여자가 낳은 사람들 가운데 세례자 요한보다 더 큰 사람은 일어나지 않았다. 그러나 천국에서 가장 작은 사람이라도 그보다 더 크다.
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 여자에게서 태어난 사람 가운데 세례자 요한보다 더 큰 사람은 나타나지 않았다. 그러나 천국에서는 가장 작은 사람이라도 요한보다 더 크다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 지금까지 세상에 태어난 사람 가운데 세례자 요한보다 더 큰 사람은 없었다. 그러나 천국에서는 가장 보잘것없는 사람이라도 요한보다 더 크다.

pt.L: Em verdade eu lhes digo: não se levantou, entre os nascidos de mulheres, [ninguém] maior que João Batista; porém o menor no Reino dos céus é maior que ele.
pt.B: Em verdade eu lhes digo: de todos os que já nasceram de mulher, não apareceu ninguém maior do que João Batista. Mesmo assim, o menor no Reino dos céus é maior do que ele.
pt.R: Eu garanto a vocês: nunca viveu ninguém maior do que João Batista. Mas até a pessoa menos importante no Reino dos céus é maior do que João.

am.L: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ ከመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ የሚበልጥ ከሴቶች በተወለዱት መካከል [ማንም] አልተነሣም፤ በመንግሥተ ሰማያት ውስጥ ያለው ታናሹ ግን ከእርሱ ይበልጣል።
am.B: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፤ ከሴት ከተወለዱት ሁሉ መካከል ከመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ የሚበልጥ ማንም አልተገለጠም። ሆኖም በመንግሥተ ሰማያት ከሁሉ ያነሰው እንኳ ከእርሱ ይበልጣል።
am.R: እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ፤ ከኖሩት ሰዎች ሁሉ ከመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ የሚበልጥ የለም። ነገር ግን በሰማይ መንግሥት ውስጥ ያለው ከሁሉ ያነሰ ሰው እንኳ ከዮሐንስ ይበልጣል።

decisions.choice: born of women: human beings
decisions.reason: The phrase means all people (Job 14:1).

decisions.choice: the least: the comparative form used as "least"
alternatives: the one who is less (or younger), meaning Jesus
decisions.reason: Greek of this period often uses the comparative for the superlative. Some early readers took "the lesser one" to be Jesus, younger than John, but the contrast is between John and anyone in the kingdom.

decisions.choice: greater: by belonging to the kingdom, not by personal worth
alternatives: John is excluded from the kingdom
decisions.reason: John announced the kingdom and stands at the turn of the ages (11:13). Those who share in it as it comes have a greater privilege than even the greatest prophet.

decisions.choice: I tell you the truth (R); Truly I tell you (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, Readable puts Jesus's solemn opening in everyday words.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's solemn "amen" before a saying, as the English has "Truly I tell you" and "I tell you the truth".

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos, at every level
decisions.reason: Matthew's own phrase, kept with its plural as the book-wide wording; it means the same as "the kingdom of God" in the other Gospels.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B), Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R); Jean le Baptiste
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9) and the French of Mark and Luke: the solemn opening in the same words at each level, and "Jean le Baptiste" without the hyphenated form, which reads as a personal name.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's solemn "amen" before a saying, as the English has "Truly I tell you" and "I tell you the truth".

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni, at every level
decisions.reason: Matthew's own phrase, kept as the book-wide wording; it means the same as "the kingdom of God" in the other Gospels.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled form for "Truly I tell you", with "các người" because Jesus is speaking to the crowds (11:7).

decisions.choice: "Giăng Báp-tít" at every level
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant title, as in Matthew 3:1; Mark 1:4 alone has Literal spell out "the one baptizing", which is a participle there and a title here.

decisions.choice: "세례자 요한"; "여자가 낳은 사람" (L), "여자에게서 태어난 사람" (B), "세상에 태어난 사람" (R); "천국" at every level
decisions.reason: "세례자 요한" as in the Korean Matthew 3:1 and Mark 1:4. Born of women means any human being (meaning decision); Readable says so.

decisions.choice: እውነት እላችኋለሁ (L, B); እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ (R)
alternatives: አሜን እላችኋለሁ (Amen I say to you)
decisions.reason: Jesus begins a solemn saying with 'Amen'. እውነት እላችኋለሁ gives its force in Amharic and is used for it through Matthew; Readable says it in the everyday form.

decisions.choice: መንግሥተ ሰማያት (L, B); የሰማይ መንግሥት (R)
decisions.reason: መንግሥተ ሰማያት is the living church name for the kingdom of heaven and keeps the Greek plural, so Literal and Balanced use it; Readable says the same in plain Amharic. The same holds in 11:12.

source.text: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν ἡμερῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ ἕως ἄρτι ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν βιάζεται, καὶ βιασταὶ ἁρπάζουσιν αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: From and the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of the heavens suffers violence, and violent [ones] seize it.

en.L: And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of the heavens suffers violence, and violent [people] seize it.
en.B: From the time of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been suffering violence, and violent people are snatching at it.
en.R: From the time John the Baptist began preaching until now, the kingdom of heaven has been attacked. Violent people are trying to take it by force.

es.L: Y desde los días de Juan el Bautista hasta ahora, el reino de los cielos es tratado con violencia, y [unos] violentos lo arrebatan.
es.B: Desde el tiempo de Juan el Bautista hasta ahora, el reino de los cielos viene sufriendo violencia, y hay gente violenta que trata de arrebatarlo.
es.R: Desde que Juan el Bautista empezó a predicar hasta ahora, el reino de los cielos ha sido atacado. Hay gente violenta que trata de apoderarse de él por la fuerza.

fr.L: Or, depuis les jours de Jean le Baptiste jusqu’à maintenant, le royaume des cieux subit la violence, et des violents s’en emparent.
fr.B: Depuis l’époque de Jean le Baptiste jusqu’à aujourd’hui, le royaume des cieux est en butte à la violence, et des violents cherchent à s’en saisir.
fr.R: Depuis le moment où Jean le Baptiste a commencé à prêcher jusqu’à maintenant, le royaume des cieux est attaqué. Des gens violents essaient de le prendre par la force.

sw.L: Tangu siku za Yohana Mbatizaji mpaka sasa, ufalme wa mbinguni unatendewa jeuri, na wajeuri wanaunyakua.
sw.B: Tangu wakati wa Yohana Mbatizaji hadi sasa, ufalme wa mbinguni umekuwa ukitendewa jeuri, na watu wenye jeuri wanajaribu kuunyakua.
sw.R: Tangu Yohana Mbatizaji alipoanza kuhubiri hadi sasa, ufalme wa mbinguni umeshambuliwa. Watu wenye jeuri wanajaribu kuuchukua kwa nguvu.

vi.L: Và từ những ngày của Giăng Báp-tít cho đến nay, vương quốc thiên đàng bị tấn công dữ dội, và những kẻ hung bạo cướp lấy nó.
vi.B: Từ thời Giăng Báp-tít cho đến nay, vương quốc thiên đàng vẫn bị tấn công dữ dội, và những kẻ hung bạo đang tìm cách cướp lấy nó.
vi.R: Từ lúc Giăng Báp-tít bắt đầu rao giảng cho đến nay, vương quốc thiên đàng bị tấn công. Những kẻ hung bạo đang tìm cách dùng sức mạnh mà chiếm lấy nó.

ko.L: 세례자 요한의 때부터 지금까지 천국은 폭행을 당하고 있고, 폭력을 쓰는 자들이 그것을 빼앗는다.
ko.B: 세례자 요한의 때부터 지금까지 천국은 폭력에 시달리고 있고, 폭력을 쓰는 사람들이 그 나라를 빼앗으려 하고 있다.
ko.R: 세례자 요한이 말씀을 전하기 시작한 때부터 지금까지 천국은 공격을 받아 왔다. 난폭한 사람들이 힘으로 그 나라를 빼앗으려고 한다.

pt.L: E, desde os dias de João Batista até agora, o Reino dos céus sofre violência, e violentos o arrebatam.
pt.B: Desde o tempo de João Batista até agora, o Reino dos céus vem sofrendo violência, e pessoas violentas tentam agarrá-lo à força.
pt.R: Desde o tempo em que João Batista começou a pregar até agora, o Reino dos céus vem sendo atacado. Pessoas violentas estão tentando tomá-lo à força.

am.L: ከመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ ቀኖችም ጀምሮ እስከ አሁን መንግሥተ ሰማያት ግፍ ይደርስባታል፤ ግፈኞችም ይነጥቋታል።
am.B: ከመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ ጊዜ አንሥቶ እስከ ዛሬ ድረስ መንግሥተ ሰማያት ጥቃት እየደረሰባት ነው፤ ዓመፀኞችም ሊነጥቋት ይሞክራሉ።
am.R: መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ መስበክ ከጀመረበት ጊዜ አንሥቶ እስከ አሁን ድረስ የሰማይ መንግሥት ጥቃት ደርሶባታል። ዓመፀኞች በኃይል ሊወስዷት ይሞክራሉ።

decisions.choice: the kingdom suffers violence, and violent people try to seize it
alternatives: the kingdom is forcefully advancing, and forceful people lay hold of it
the kingdom is entered by force, as Luke 16:16 says everyone forces their way in
decisions.reason: The verb can be passive ("suffers violence") or middle ("advances with force"), and the second clause can be hostile or eager. This verse is among the hardest in Matthew. The noun "violent people" and the verb "seize" are usually negative, and John is in prison, so the hostile reading is taken here.

decisions.choice: from the days of John until now: since John began to preach
decisions.reason: John's ministry marks the start of the new time (11:13). His arrest (4:12; 14:3-10) and the rising opposition to Jesus (9:34; 10:16-25) show the kingdom under attack.

decisions.choice: has been suffering violence (B); has been attacked (R)
decisions.reason: The present tense describes something going on from John's days until now.

decisions.choice: the time John the Baptist began preaching
alternatives: the days of John the Baptist
decisions.reason: Readable says which days are meant.

decisions.choice: es tratado con violencia (L); viene sufriendo violencia (B); ha sido atacado (R)
decisions.reason: Every level takes the verb as passive, the kingdom suffering violence, as the meaning decision does (m1, uncertain); the other reading, that the kingdom forces its way ahead, is set out there.

decisions.choice: unatendewa jeuri (L); umekuwa ukitendewa jeuri (B); umeshambuliwa (R)
decisions.reason: Every level takes the verb as passive, the kingdom suffering violence, as the meaning decision does (m1, uncertain); the other reading, that the kingdom forces its way ahead, is set out there.

decisions.choice: "bị tấn công dữ dội"; "những kẻ hung bạo cướp lấy nó"
alternatives: "được tiến triển mạnh mẽ, và người mạnh mẽ chiếm lấy"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as passive, the kingdom suffering violence, and footnotes the other reading; Vietnamese follows that reading at every level, so the footnote carries the alternative.

decisions.choice: "폭행을 당하다" (L), "폭력에 시달리다" (B), "공격을 받다" (R); "빼앗다"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision (footnoted) reads the verb as passive: the kingdom suffers violence from violent people. "침노" is the word of older versions and is no longer understood; the reading that the kingdom forcefully advances is the alternative in the footnote.

source.text: πάντες γὰρ οἱ προφῆται καὶ ὁ νόμος ἕως Ἰωάννου ἐπροφήτευσαν·

records.literal_gloss: All for the prophets and the law until John prophesied;

en.L: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
en.B: For all the prophets and the law spoke of what was coming, until John.
en.R: All the prophets and the law of Moses told about what was going to happen, until John came.

es.L: Porque todos los profetas y la ley, hasta Juan, profetizaron.
es.B: Porque todos los profetas y la ley anunciaban lo que había de venir, hasta que llegó Juan.
es.R: Todos los profetas y la ley de Moisés hablaban de lo que iba a pasar, hasta que vino Juan.

fr.L: Car tous les prophètes et la Loi ont prophétisé jusqu’à Jean.
fr.B: Car tous les prophètes et la Loi ont annoncé ce qui devait venir, jusqu’à Jean.
fr.R: Tous les prophètes et la Loi de Moïse ont parlé de ce qui allait arriver, jusqu’à la venue de Jean.

sw.L: Kwa maana manabii wote na sheria, hadi Yohana, walitoa unabii.
sw.B: Kwa maana manabii wote na sheria walinena juu ya mambo yajayo, mpaka Yohana.
sw.R: Manabii wote na sheria ya Musa walieleza mambo ambayo yangetokea, mpaka Yohana alipokuja.

vi.L: Vì tất cả các nhà tiên tri và luật pháp đều đã nói tiên tri cho đến Giăng.
vi.B: Vì tất cả các nhà tiên tri và luật pháp đều đã nói trước về điều sẽ đến, cho đến thời Giăng.
vi.R: Tất cả các nhà tiên tri và luật pháp Môi-se đều đã nói trước về những việc sẽ xảy ra, cho đến khi Giăng đến.

ko.L: 모든 예언자들과 율법이 요한까지 예언하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 모든 예언자와 율법은 요한 때까지 앞으로 올 일을 예언하였다.
ko.R: 모든 예언자와 모세의 율법은 요한이 올 때까지 앞으로 일어날 일을 미리 말해 주었다.

pt.L: Pois todos os profetas e a Lei profetizaram até João.
pt.B: Pois todos os profetas e a Lei falaram do que estava por vir, até João.
pt.R: Todos os profetas e a Lei de Moisés falaram do que ia acontecer, até João chegar.

am.L: ሁሉም ነቢያትና ሕጉ እስከ ዮሐንስ ትንቢት ተናገሩና።
am.B: ሁሉም ነቢያትና ሕጉ ዮሐንስ እስኪመጣ ድረስ ስለሚመጣው ነገር ተናግረዋልና።
am.R: ነቢያት ሁሉና የሙሴ ሕግ ዮሐንስ እስኪመጣ ድረስ ወደፊት ስለሚሆነው ነገር ተናገሩ።

decisions.choice: prophesied: pointed ahead to the coming kingdom
decisions.reason: Until John the Scriptures looked forward; with John the time of fulfillment begins. Jesus does not set the law aside (5:17-18).

decisions.choice: the prophets and the law: an unusual order
alternatives: the usual "the law and the prophets"
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Matthew writes "the law and the prophets" (5:17; 7:12). Putting the prophets first stresses that even the law spoke of what was to come.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Readable says which law is meant.

decisions.choice: la Loi, capitalised
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9): the Law of Moses is "la Loi"; Readable adds "de Moïse" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "예언자들과 율법" in Matthew's unusual order
decisions.reason: The order is unusual (meaning decision) and Korean can keep it at every level; Readable names the law of Moses, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ εἰ θέλετε δέξασθαι, αὐτός ἐστιν Ἠλίας ὁ μέλλων ἔρχεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And if you are willing to receive [it], he is Elijah the one about to come.

en.L: And if you are willing to accept [it], he is Elijah, who is to come.
en.B: And, if you will receive it, John is Elijah, whose coming was foretold.
en.R: If you are willing to accept this, John is the Elijah that God said would come.

es.L: Y si {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} recibir [esto], él es Elías, el que va a venir.
es.B: Y, si {{plural_you:están|estáis}} dispuestos a recibirlo, Juan es Elías, cuya venida estaba anunciada.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} aceptar esto, Juan es el Elías que Dios dijo que vendría.

fr.L: Et si vous voulez [l’]accepter, c’est lui, Élie, qui doit venir.
fr.B: Et, si vous voulez bien l’admettre, Jean est cet Élie dont la venue avait été annoncée.
fr.R: Si vous êtes prêts à accepter cela, Jean est l’Élie dont Dieu avait dit qu’il viendrait.

sw.L: Na ikiwa mnapenda kupokea [hili], yeye ni Eliya yule aliyepaswa kuja.
sw.B: Na ikiwa mko tayari kulipokea, Yohana ndiye Eliya ambaye kuja kwake kulitabiriwa.
sw.R: Kama mko tayari kukubali jambo hili, Yohana ndiye yule Eliya ambaye Mungu alisema angekuja.

vi.L: Và nếu các người muốn chấp nhận, thì chính ông là Ê-li, người phải đến.
vi.B: Nếu các người chịu chấp nhận điều này, thì Giăng chính là Ê-li, người đã được báo trước là sẽ đến.
vi.R: Nếu các người chịu tin điều này, thì Giăng chính là Ê-li mà Đức Chúa Trời đã nói là sẽ đến.

ko.L: 그리고 너희가 받아들이기를 원한다면, 그가 오기로 되어 있는 엘리야이다.
ko.B: 너희가 받아들이려고 한다면, 요한이 바로 오기로 되어 있던 엘리야이다.
ko.R: 너희가 이 말을 받아들이려고 한다면, 요한이 바로 하나님께서 보내시겠다고 하신 그 엘리야이다.

pt.L: E, se vocês quiserem aceitar [isso], ele é Elias, que está para vir.
pt.B: E, se vocês quiserem aceitar, João é o Elias cuja vinda foi anunciada.
pt.R: Se vocês quiserem aceitar isto: João é o Elias que Deus disse que viria.

am.L: ለመቀበልም ፈቃደኞች ብትሆኑ፣ እርሱ ሊመጣ ያለው ኤልያስ ነው።
am.B: ልትቀበሉት ብትፈልጉ፣ ዮሐንስ መምጣቱ አስቀድሞ የተነገረለት ኤልያስ ነው።
am.R: ይህን ለመቀበል ፈቃደኞች ከሆናችሁ፣ እግዚአብሔር ይመጣል ያለው ኤልያስ ዮሐንስ ነው።

decisions.choice: Elijah who is to come: Malachi 4:5
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5; 3:23 in the Hebrew). Jesus says the same in 17:10-13.

decisions.choice: he is Elijah: John fulfills Elijah's role
decisions.reason: In John 1:21 the Baptist denies that he is Elijah himself. He comes "in the spirit and power of Elijah" (Luke 1:17).

decisions.choice: if you are willing to accept it: the claim needs an open heart
decisions.reason: Many expected Elijah himself. Seeing John as the promised Elijah means seeing Jesus as the one who follows.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, since Jesus has just spoken of the law and the prophets.

decisions.choice: "Ê-li"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration used in the style guide and Mark 9:11-13.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.

records.literal_gloss: The one having ears let him hear.

en.L: The one who has ears, let him hear.
en.B: Whoever has ears must listen.
en.R: If you can hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, pay attention to this!

es.L: El que tiene oídos, que oiga.
es.B: Quien tenga oídos, que escuche.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} oír lo que digo, ¡{{plural_you:presten|prestad}} atención a esto!

fr.L: Celui qui a des oreilles, qu’il entende !
fr.B: Que celui qui a des oreilles écoute !
fr.R: Si vous pouvez {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}entendre, faites bien attention à cela !

sw.L: Aliye na masikio, na asikie.
sw.B: Yeyote mwenye masikio, na asikilize.
sw.R: Kama mnaweza kunisikia, sikilizeni jambo hili kwa makini!

vi.L: Ai có tai, hãy nghe.
vi.B: Ai có tai thì hãy lắng nghe.
vi.R: Ai nghe được {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì hãy chú ý đến lời này!

ko.L: 귀가 있는 사람은 들어라.
ko.B: 귀가 있는 사람은 잘 들어라.
ko.R: 내 말을 들을 수 있는 사람은 이 말을 잘 새겨들어라!

pt.L: Quem tem ouvidos, ouça.
pt.B: Quem tem ouvidos, que escute.
pt.R: Se vocês conseguem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouvir, prestem atenção nisto!

am.L: ጆሮ ያለው ይስማ።
am.B: ጆሮ ያለው ሁሉ ያዳምጥ።
am.R: እኔን መስማት የምትችሉ ከሆነ ይህን በጥንቃቄ አድምጡ!

decisions.choice: whoever has ears, let him hear: a call to listen closely and take the saying to heart
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same words after other sayings that need thought (13:9, 43).

decisions.choice: If you can hear me, pay attention to this!
alternatives: The one who has ears, let him hear
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the saying in plain words.

decisions.choice: oír lo que digo, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Readable "hear me" takes the setting; Spanish says "what I say", with no pronoun for Jesus to capitalise.

decisions.choice: "Ai có tai, hãy nghe" (L); "Ai có tai thì hãy lắng nghe" (B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: As Mark 4:9: "ai" (whoever) already includes men and women. Readable follows the English Readable's sense.

decisions.choice: "귀가 있는 사람은 들어라" (L), "잘 들어라" (B), spelled out (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew has only "ears" where Mark has "ears to hear", so the Korean leaves out "들을"; Balanced adds "잘" as the Korean Mark 4:9 does. It is a call to take the saying to heart (meaning decision), which Readable says.

source.text: Τίνι δὲ ὁμοιώσω τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην;

records.literal_gloss: To what but will I compare the generation this?

en.L: But to what shall I compare this generation?
en.B: What picture shall I use for the people of this generation?
en.R: How can I describe the people living today?

es.L: Pero ¿con qué compararé a esta generación?
es.B: ¿Con qué imagen describiré a la gente de esta generación?
es.R: ¿Cómo puedo describir a la gente de hoy?

fr.L: Mais à quoi comparerai-je cette génération ?
fr.B: À quelle image vais-je comparer les gens de cette génération ?
fr.R: Comment est-ce que je peux décrire les gens d’aujourd’hui ?

sw.L: Lakini kizazi hiki nitakifananisha na nini?
sw.B: Nitatumia mfano gani kuwaeleza watu wa kizazi hiki?
sw.R: Niwaelezeje watu wanaoishi siku hizi?

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ so sánh thế hệ này với gì?
vi.B: Ta biết lấy gì để ví thế hệ này?
vi.R: Ta biết nói thế nào về những người sống thời nay?

ko.L: 그런데 이 세대를 무엇에 비길까?
ko.B: 이 세대 사람들을 무엇에 비길 수 있을까?
ko.R: 요즘 사람들을 무엇에 비길 수 있을까?

pt.L: Mas a que compararei esta geração?
pt.B: Com que imagem vou descrever as pessoas desta geração?
pt.R: Como posso descrever as pessoas que vivem hoje?

am.L: ይህንን ትውልድ በምን እመስለዋለሁ?
am.B: የዚህን ትውልድ ሰዎች በምን ልመስላቸው?
am.R: በዛሬ ጊዜ ያሉትን ሰዎች እንዴት ልግለጻቸው?

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus's day, taken as a whole
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase of the people who rejected both John and himself (12:39-45; 23:36).

decisions.choice: "thế hệ này" (L, B); "những người sống thời nay" (R)
decisions.reason: The people of Jesus's day taken as a whole (meaning decision), as in Mark 8:38 and 13:30.

decisions.choice: "이 세대" (L), "이 세대 사람들" (B), "요즘 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The people of Jesus's day taken as a whole (meaning decision); "이 세대" as in the Korean Mark 8:12 and 13:30.

source.text: ὁμοία ἐστὶν παιδίοις καθημένοις ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἃ προσφωνοῦντα τοῖς ἑτέροις λέγουσιν· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκόψασθε·

records.literal_gloss: Like it is to children sitting in the marketplaces who calling out to the others \v 17 say, We piped for you and not you danced; we lamented and not you beat [your breasts];

en.L: It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to the others, \v 17 saying, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not beat [your breasts].'
en.B: They are like children who sit in the town squares and call out to the other children, \v 17 'We played the pipe for you, but you did not dance; we sang a funeral song, but you did not beat your breasts in grief.'
en.R: They are like children sitting in the marketplace. They call out to the other children, \v 17 'We played happy music for you, but you would not dance. We sang sad songs for you, but you would not cry.'

es.L: Es semejante a niños sentados en las plazas que, gritando a los otros, \v 17 dicen: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos la flauta, y no {{plural_you:bailaron|bailasteis}}; entonamos lamentos, y no {{plural_you:se golpearon|os golpeasteis}} [el pecho]”.
es.B: Son como niños que se sientan en las plazas y les gritan a los otros niños: \v 17 “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos la flauta, pero no {{plural_you:bailaron|bailasteis}}; cantamos canciones de duelo, pero no {{plural_you:se golpearon|os golpeasteis}} el pecho de dolor”.
es.R: Son como niños sentados en la plaza del mercado. Les gritan a los otros niños: \v 17 “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos música alegre, pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} bailar. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} cantamos canciones tristes, pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} llorar”.

fr.L: Elle est semblable à des enfants assis sur les places, qui interpellent les autres, \v 17 disant : “Nous avons joué de la flûte pour vous, et vous n’avez pas dansé ; nous avons chanté un chant de deuil, et vous ne vous êtes pas frappé [la poitrine].”
fr.B: Ils ressemblent à des enfants assis sur les places, qui crient aux autres enfants : \v 17 “Nous avons joué de la flûte pour vous, et vous n’avez pas dansé ; nous avons chanté un chant funèbre, et vous ne vous êtes pas frappé la poitrine en signe de deuil.”
fr.R: Ils sont comme des enfants assis sur la place du marché. Ils crient aux autres enfants : \v 17 “Nous avons joué une musique joyeuse pour vous, mais vous n’avez pas voulu danser. Nous avons chanté des chants tristes pour vous, mais vous n’avez pas voulu pleurer.”

sw.L: Kinafanana na watoto wanaokaa katika viwanja vya soko, wanaowaita wale wengine, \v 17 wakisema, 'Tuliwapigia zumari, nanyi hamkucheza; tuliimba nyimbo za maombolezo, nanyi hamkujipiga [vifua].'
sw.B: Wao ni kama watoto wanaokaa viwanjani na kuwaita watoto wenzao, \v 17 'Tuliwapigia zumari, lakini hamkucheza; tuliimba wimbo wa msiba, lakini hamkujipiga vifua kwa huzuni.'
sw.R: Wao ni kama watoto walioketi sokoni. Wanawaita watoto wengine, \v 17 'Tuliwapigia muziki wa furaha, lakini hamkutaka kucheza. Tuliwaimbia nyimbo za huzuni, lakini hamkutaka kulia.'

vi.L: Nó giống như trẻ con ngồi ở các chợ, gọi những đứa khác \v 17 và nói: 'Chúng tôi đã thổi sáo cho các bạn, mà các bạn không nhảy múa; chúng tôi đã hát bài ai ca, mà các bạn không đấm ngực khóc than.'
vi.B: Họ giống như những đứa trẻ ngồi ngoài chợ, gọi các bạn khác: \v 17 'Chúng tôi thổi sáo cho các bạn, mà các bạn chẳng chịu nhảy múa; chúng tôi hát bài tang chế, mà các bạn chẳng chịu đấm ngực khóc than.'
vi.R: Họ giống như những đứa trẻ ngồi chơi ở chợ. Chúng gọi các bạn khác: \v 17 'Bọn mình thổi sáo vui cho các bạn, mà các bạn không chịu nhảy múa. Bọn mình hát bài buồn cho các bạn, mà các bạn không chịu khóc.'

ko.L: 그것은 장터에 앉아서 다른 아이들에게 소리쳐 \v 17 말하는 아이들과 같다. '우리가 너희에게 피리를 불어도 너희는 춤추지 않았고, 우리가 애곡해도 너희는 가슴을 치지 않았다.'
ko.B: 그들은 장터에 앉아서 다른 아이들에게 이렇게 소리치는 아이들과 같다. \v 17 '우리가 너희를 위해 피리를 불었는데도 너희는 춤을 추지 않았고, 우리가 장례 노래를 불렀는데도 너희는 가슴을 치며 울지 않았다.'
ko.R: 그들은 장터에 앉아 있는 아이들과 같다. 그 아이들은 다른 아이들에게 소리친다. \v 17 '우리가 신나는 피리를 불어 주었는데, 너희는 춤을 추지 않았다. 우리가 슬픈 노래를 불러 주었는데, 너희는 울지 않았다.'

pt.L: É semelhante a crianças sentadas nas praças, que gritam para os outros, \v 17 dizendo: 'Tocamos flauta para vocês, e vocês não dançaram; cantamos um lamento, e vocês não bateram [no peito].'
pt.B: São como crianças sentadas nas praças da cidade, que gritam para as outras crianças: \v 17 'Tocamos flauta para vocês, mas vocês não dançaram; cantamos um canto fúnebre, mas vocês não bateram no peito de tristeza.'
pt.R: Elas são como crianças sentadas na praça. Elas gritam para as outras crianças: \v 17 'Tocamos música alegre para vocês, mas vocês não quiseram dançar. Cantamos músicas tristes para vocês, mas vocês não quiseram chorar.'

am.L: በገበያ ስፍራዎች ተቀምጠው ሌሎቹን የሚጣሩ ልጆችን ይመስላል፤ \v 17 እንዲህም ይላሉ፦ “ዋሽንት ነፋንላችሁ፤ አልጨፈራችሁምም፤ የሐዘን ዜማ አዜምንላችሁ፤ [ደረታችሁንም] አልመታችሁም።”
am.B: በከተማው አደባባይ ተቀምጠው ሌሎቹን ልጆች የሚጣሩ ልጆችን ይመስላሉ፤ \v 17 “ዋሽንት ነፋንላችሁ፤ እናንተ ግን አልጨፈራችሁም፤ የለቅሶ ዜማ አዜምን፤ እናንተ ግን ደረታችሁን እየመታችሁ አላለቀሳችሁም።”
am.R: በገበያ ቦታ የተቀመጡ ልጆችን ይመስላሉ። ሌሎቹን ልጆች ይጣራሉ፤ \v 17 “የደስታ ሙዚቃ ተጫወትንላችሁ፤ እናንተ ግን አልጨፈራችሁም። የሐዘን ዘፈን ዘፈንላችሁ፤ እናንተ ግን አላለቀሳችሁም።”

decisions.choice: children's games of wedding and funeral
decisions.reason: Children copied adult life in the public square: the flute and dancing of a wedding, the laments and breast-beating of mourners.

decisions.choice: the children who call out stand for this generation, who wanted John and Jesus to play their tune
alternatives: the calling children are John and Jesus, and this generation would not respond
decisions.reason: "This generation" is like the children who call out. 11:18-19 then shows them finding fault with both John's fasting and Jesus's feasting.

decisions.choice: played happy music; sang sad songs
alternatives: played the flute; sang a lament
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of music each was.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans in the children's words
decisions.reason: The children speak to the other children, a plural "you", so their words take the setting like Jesus's own.

decisions.choice: "bài ai ca" (L); "bài tang chế" (B); "đấm ngực khóc than" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The children's games of wedding and funeral (meaning decision): mourners beat their breasts, so Literal and Balanced say so; Readable has "bọn mình", the way children talk.

decisions.choice: "소리쳐 \v 17 말하는" (L); the verb of saying placed before the marker (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb of saying at the end of its clause, after what is said; Literal keeps "saying" after the 11:17 marker as the Greek has it, and Balanced and Readable finish the sentence in 11:16 so that the children's words begin 11:17. The games of wedding and funeral (meaning decision) are spelled out in Readable.

decisions.choice: as praças
decisions.reason: The place was the open public square where people met and traded, and where children played (m1). In Brazil that is "a praça"; "mercado" suggests a covered market building.

decisions.choice: the comparison ends verse 16, and the children's words follow in verse 17
alternatives: one sentence ending with ይመስላል after the children's words, which would move verse 16's main verb into verse 17
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the main verb last. To keep each verse's own words after its number, verse 16 closes with 'it is like children ... who call out' and verse 17 begins with what they say.

source.text: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης μήτε ἐσθίων μήτε πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·

records.literal_gloss: Came for John neither eating nor drinking, and they say, A demon he has.

en.L: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
en.B: For when John came, he did not eat or drink as others do, and people say, 'There is a demon in him.'
en.R: John went without food and did not drink wine. And people say, 'A demon has control of him!'

es.L: Porque llegó Juan sin comer ni beber, y dicen: “Tiene un demonio”.
es.B: Porque vino Juan, que no comía ni bebía como los demás, y la gente dice: “Tiene un demonio dentro”.
es.R: Juan ayunaba y no tomaba vino. Y la gente dice: “¡Un demonio lo controla!”.

fr.L: Car Jean est venu, ne mangeant ni ne buvant, et ils disent : “Il a un démon.”
fr.B: En effet, Jean est venu ; il ne mangeait pas et ne buvait pas comme les autres, et l’on dit : “Il y a un démon en lui.”
fr.R: Jean ne mangeait pas comme les autres et il ne buvait pas de vin. Et les gens disent : “Un démon le contrôle !”

sw.L: Kwa maana Yohana alikuja bila kula wala kunywa, nao wanasema, 'Ana pepo.'
sw.B: Kwa maana Yohana alipokuja, hakula wala kunywa kama wengine, na watu wanasema, 'Ana pepo ndani yake.'
sw.R: Yohana alifunga kula, wala hakunywa divai. Na watu wanasema, 'Pepo amemtawala!'

vi.L: Vì Giăng đến, không ăn cũng không uống, thì người ta nói: 'Ông ấy bị quỷ ám.'
vi.B: Vì Giăng đến, không ăn không uống như người thường, thì người ta nói: 'Ông ấy bị quỷ ám.'
vi.R: Giăng nhịn ăn và không uống rượu, thì người ta nói: 'Ông ấy bị quỷ điều khiển!'

ko.L: 요한이 와서 먹지도 않고 마시지도 않으니, 그들이 '그는 귀신이 들렸다' 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 요한이 와서 남들처럼 먹지도 마시지도 않으니, 사람들이 '그는 귀신이 들렸다' 하고 말한다.
ko.R: 요한은 음식을 먹지 않고 포도주도 마시지 않았다. 그러자 사람들이 '저 사람은 귀신에게 사로잡혔다!' 하고 말한다.

pt.L: Pois veio João, nem comendo nem bebendo, e dizem: 'Ele tem demônio.'
pt.B: Pois, quando João veio, não comia nem bebia como os outros, e as pessoas dizem: 'Há um demônio nele.'
pt.R: João ficava sem comer e não bebia vinho. E as pessoas dizem: 'Ele está dominado por um demônio!'

am.L: ዮሐንስ ሳይበላም ሳይጠጣም መጥቷልና፤ “ጋኔን አለበት” ይላሉም።
am.B: ዮሐንስ በመጣ ጊዜ እንደ ሌሎች ሰዎች አልበላም አልጠጣምም፤ ሰዎችም “ጋኔን አድሮበታል” ይላሉ።
am.R: ዮሐንስ ምግብ ሳይበላና የወይን ጠጅ ሳይጠጣ ኖረ። ሰዎችም “ጋኔን ተቆጣጥሮታል!” ይላሉ።

decisions.choice: neither eating nor drinking: John's strict, simple life
alternatives: he ate and drank nothing at all
decisions.reason: John lived on locusts and wild honey (3:4), fasted (9:14), and drank no wine (Luke 1:15).

decisions.choice: he has a demon: he is mad, controlled by an evil spirit
decisions.reason: The charge was a way of dismissing someone as out of his mind (John 10:20).

decisions.choice: as others do (B); went without food and did not drink wine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that ordinary meals and wine are meant.

decisions.choice: "귀신이 들렸다" (L, B); "귀신에게 사로잡혔다" (R)
decisions.reason: "He has a demon" means he is mad, controlled by an evil spirit (meaning decision); Korean keeps the charge as it was spoken, with "귀신" as through Matthew.

source.text: ἦλθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, τελωνῶν φίλος καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Came the Son of the Man eating and drinking, and they say, Behold, a man glutton and drunkard, of tax collectors friend and of sinners.

en.L: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look, a man [who is] a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
en.B: The Son of Man came and ate and drank, and they say, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
en.R: The Son of Man came, eating and drinking with people. And they say, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much wine. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

es.L: Vino el Hijo del Hombre comiendo y bebiendo, y dicen: “Ahí está: un hombre glotón y bebedor, amigo de publicanos y de pecadores”.
es.B: Llegó el Hijo del Hombre, que sí come y bebe, y dicen: “¡{{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}! Come demasiado y bebe demasiado, y es amigo de cobradores de impuestos y de pecadores”.
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre vino y come y bebe con la gente. Y dicen: “¡{{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}! Come demasiado y bebe demasiado vino. ¡Es amigo de cobradores de impuestos y de pecadores!”.

fr.L: Le Fils de l’homme est venu, mangeant et buvant, et ils disent : “Voici un homme glouton et ivrogne, ami des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs !”
fr.B: Le Fils de l’homme est venu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a mangé et bu, et l’on dit : “Regardez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! Il mange trop et boit trop, et c’est un ami des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs !”
fr.R: Le Fils de l’homme est venu, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a mangé et bu avec les gens. Et les gens disent : “Regardez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! Il mange trop et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} boit trop de vin. C’est un ami des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs !”

sw.L: Mwana wa Adamu alikuja akila na kunywa, nao wanasema, 'Tazameni, mtu mlafi na mlevi, rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'
sw.B: Mwana wa Adamu alikuja akila na kunywa, nao wanasema, 'Mwangalieni! Anakula kupita kiasi, anakunywa kupita kiasi, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu alikuja, akala na kunywa pamoja na watu. Nao wanasema, 'Mwangalieni! Anakula kupita kiasi na kunywa divai kupita kiasi. Ni rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'

vi.L: Con Người đến, cũng ăn cũng uống, thì người ta nói: 'Kìa, một kẻ ham ăn và nghiện rượu, bạn của người thu thuế và người tội lỗi!'
vi.B: Con Người đến, ăn uống như mọi người, thì người ta nói: 'Hãy xem người này! Ăn nhiều, uống nhiều, lại là bạn của người thu thuế và người tội lỗi!'
vi.R: Con Người đến, cùng ăn cùng uống với người ta, thì họ nói: 'Hãy nhìn người này! Ăn uống quá độ, lại còn uống nhiều rượu. Người này là bạn của người thu thuế và người tội lỗi!'

ko.L: 인자가 와서 먹고 마시니, 그들이 '보라, 먹기를 좋아하고 술을 즐기는 사람, 세리들과 죄인들의 친구다!' 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 인자가 와서 먹고 마시니, 사람들이 '저 사람을 보아라! 너무 많이 먹고 너무 많이 마신다. 세리들과 죄인들의 친구다!' 하고 말한다.
ko.R: 인자는 와서 사람들과 함께 먹고 마셨다. 그러자 사람들이 '저 사람 좀 봐라! 음식을 너무 많이 먹고 포도주를 너무 많이 마신다. 세리와 죄인들하고 친구로 지낸다!' 하고 말한다.

pt.L: Veio o Filho do Homem comendo e bebendo, e dizem: 'Eis um homem comilão e beberrão, amigo de cobradores de impostos e de pecadores!'
pt.B: O Filho do Homem veio, comeu e bebeu, e dizem: 'Olhem só para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}! Come demais e bebe demais, e é amigo de cobradores de impostos e de pecadores!'

decisions.choice: a glutton and a drunkard: the charge against a rebellious son
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes the rebellious son in Deuteronomy 21:20 (in the Greek version), who was to be put to death.

decisions.choice: friend of tax collectors and sinners: Jesus ate with them
decisions.reason: See 9:10-11. Eating together was a sign of acceptance.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Jesus's way of speaking of himself (8:20; 9:6).

decisions.choice: look (L); look at him (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: he is (B)
decisions.reason: "A man" is the speakers' scornful way of pointing at Jesus. Balanced says "he". Inside the speakers' words the pronoun still refers to Jesus, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting except at the start of a sentence.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m3), a title, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: publicanos (L); cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal keeps the traditional word, Balanced and Readable say what these men did.

decisions.choice: le Fils de l’homme, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 5): a title of Jesus, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m3), as in John; never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "một kẻ" (L); "người này" (B, R) in the accusers' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Those who speak are mocking Jesus, so they use the plain "người này", as the scribes do in 9:3; a pronoun of reverence would not suit their words, and "người này" takes no setting span where the English Balanced and Readable have one.

decisions.choice: the critics speak of Jesus as "사람" and "저 사람" without honorific
decisions.reason: They speak against him, so Korean gives them no honorific for him, as with the Pharisees in 9:34; the narrator and Jesus's own words keep "인자" plain, since a Korean speaker does not honor himself.

decisions.choice: "먹기를 좋아하고 술을 즐기는 사람" (L); "너무 많이 먹고 너무 많이 마신다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The charge echoes the one against a rebellious son (meaning decision); the Korean describes what they accuse him of rather than using a familiar version's pair of nouns.

decisions.choice: ሆዳምና ሰካራም (a glutton and a drunkard)
alternatives: በላተኛና ጠጪ (an eater and a drinker)
decisions.reason: ሆዳም and ሰካራም are the everyday Amharic insults for one who overeats and one who drinks too much, which is the force of the two Greek words; 'eater' and 'drinker' would not sound like an accusation.

decisions.choice: her deeds, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: her children, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "children", as Luke 7:35 does. The earliest witnesses of Matthew are thought to read "deeds", and copyists probably brought Matthew into line with Luke. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: wisdom: God's wise purpose, seen in the ways of John and of Jesus
decisions.reason: Wisdom is pictured as a woman, as in Proverbs 8-9. Her deeds are the works of the Messiah (11:2), the same word in Greek, which frames this section.

decisions.choice: was vindicated: a past tense stating a general truth
decisions.reason: The past tense here states what always proves to be so; Balanced and Readable use the present.

decisions.choice: vindicated (L); show that she is in the right (B); shows that wisdom is right (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means shown to be in the right. "Justified" would suggest being forgiven.

decisions.choice: fue reivindicada
decisions.reason: Shown to be in the right (meaning decision m3). "Justificada" in Spanish now usually means excused.

decisions.choice: a été justifiée (L)
decisions.reason: The English avoids "justified", which suggests being forgiven. In ordinary French "justifier" means to show that someone was right, so Literal can keep it, as in Luke 7:35; Balanced and Readable say the same thing plainly.

decisions.choice: ilionyeshwa kuwa sahihi (L); inaonyesha kwamba iko sahihi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Shown to be in the right (meaning decision m3). "Kuhesabiwa haki" is the phrase for being made righteous before God, and "haki" is kept for righteousness, so it would point the wrong way here.

decisions.choice: "sự khôn ngoan" with "nó" (L)
decisions.reason: Wisdom here is God's wise purpose, seen in John and in Jesus (meaning decision), not a title; Vietnamese has no feminine pronoun, so the English "her" becomes "nó" at Literal and the noun is repeated elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "옳다고 인정되었다" (L); "옳다는 것이 드러난다" (B); "옳다는 것을 알 수 있다" (R)
decisions.reason: The past tense states a general truth (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable use the present; Literal keeps the past. "의롭다 함을 받다" is the Korean of Paul's teaching on justification and would mislead here. Wisdom is God's wise purpose (meaning decision), seen in John and Jesus.

decisions.choice: foi comprovada pelas suas obras (L); as obras ... mostram que ela tem razão (B); o que a sabedoria faz mostra que ela está certa (R)
decisions.reason: Section 6 of the style guide keeps "justificar" for this verb in Paul, where it means God declaring someone righteous; here, as the English decision says, it means shown to be in the right, which "comprovada" says. "Obras" at Literal and Balanced repeats "as obras do Cristo" of 11:2, the frame the meaning note (m2) points out.

decisions.choice: ጸደቀች (was shown to be right)
decisions.reason: ጸደቀ is the verb of the same family as ጽድቅ, righteousness, and means to be shown to be in the right, which is the Greek verb's sense here; Balanced and Readable say it in plain words, as the English does.
